services.title: Services | Design, Integration & Maintenance | Solomon Radclyffe
services.description: Consulting and risk advisory, design and analysis, installation and integration, and maintenance and support with one-year DLP, SLAs and lifecycle management.
services.h1: Turnkey design, installation and lifecycle support
services.lead: One contract from first survey to end of life: consulting and risk advice, design and engineering, installation and integration, then maintenance and support for as long as you run the systems.

sections.h2: Four service lines, one delivery team
sections.intro: Many integrators sell equipment and subcontract the work. We keep consulting, design, installation and maintenance inside the same business, so the engineer who surveyed your site is still accountable for it years later.

items.p: Threat and vulnerability assessment, security master planning and technology roadmaps for estates that will be built in phases. You get a defensible basis for spending the budget in the right order.
System design, device schedules, drawings and specifications issued for tender or construction, with the interfaces between systems worked out on paper before anyone drills a hole.
Our own engineers install, configure and commission the works, including civils, containment, cabling and the links into the systems you already run.
Preventive schedules, contracted response times and spares held for the critical devices on your site, so the system you bought still performs in year five.

sections.h2: What a project asks of you, and what you get back
sections.intro: Three stages, three sets of deliverables. Most clients spend a few hours with us at each stage rather than weeks.

items.p: We agree the objective, then survey the site: existing systems, coverage gaps, power and network routes, and the operational reality your team works in.
You receive drawings, device schedules and a fixed scope of works, with the equipment options costed side by side and ready for procurement or board approval.
We install and commission with as little disruption to operations as possible, train your team, hand over as-built records, and stay on beyond the Defects Liability Period.

images.alt: Technician uses a tablet and screwdriver to inspect wiring inside an open electrical control cabinet.

sections.h2: A system is only as good as the year it fails
sections.intro: Equipment drifts. Cameras lose focus, door contacts stick, drives age. We plan for that from day one, so faults are found on a schedule rather than in an incident review.
bullets: A one-year Defects Liability Period on every installation, with faults rectified at our cost
Contracted response times and spares held for the critical devices on your site
Lifecycle planning that tells you when equipment should be replaced rather than repaired again

sections.h2: The questions procurement teams ask
sections.intro: Straight answers to what comes up late in evaluation. If your question is not here, ask it and we will answer it plainly.

items.h: Can you work with the systems we already have?
items.p: Yes, and it is often the cheapest route. We survey what is installed, keep what is serviceable, and design the new work around it. Where a system is at end of life we say so, with the cost of keeping it set against the cost of replacing it.

items.h: Are you tied to one manufacturer?
items.p: No. We are vendor independent and accredited on the platforms we deploy, so the specification follows your risk and your budget rather than a distribution agreement. Licences and records stay with you.

items.h: How do we buy from you?
items.p: Directly, or through the route your organisation already uses: tender, framework, or as a nominated subcontractor to a main contractor. We work alongside consultants and main contractors regularly and are used to their documentation.

items.h: What happens in the first conversation?
items.p: A scoping call with the engineer who would deliver the work, not a sales call. We ask about the site, the risk you are carrying and the timeline, then tell you honestly whether a survey is worth commissioning.

sections.h2: Start with a conversation, not a quotation
sections.intro: Send us the site and the objective. You will speak to the engineer who would deliver the work, and get an honest view of what it takes.

Lane, reader and turnstile layout planned around real peak flows — a shift change, a morning intake — rather than a theoretical throughput figure.

items.h: Tied into what you already run

sections.intro: Founded in the UAE as RGS Global Security

sections.h2: Two decades of delivery, under one board
sections.intro: RGS Global Security was founded in the UAE in 2007 and expanded into Africa in 2010 as RGS Africa. Solomon Radclyffe brings those operations together: one privately held group, one board, one standard of delivery across every office.

images.alt: Two IT technicians inspect a blurred tablet beside network server racks in a cable-filled server room.

sections.h2: One team from survey to handover
sections.intro: Every project runs through the same four stages, with the same accountable team. You know who is responsible at each step and what happens next.

items.p: We walk the site, record what already exists and agree the risks that matter before anything is priced.
Drawings, equipment schedules and system interfaces documented so the design can be built, maintained and audited.
Our own engineers install, test and commission to the specification, and you can see progress as it happens.
The people who will operate the system are trained on it, and every drawing and licence is handed over.

sections.h2: Tell us what you are protecting
sections.intro: A single conversation is usually enough for us to tell you whether we are the right integrator for the site, and what we would do first.

heroImages.alt: Two maintenance workers in navy uniforms examine a tablet inside an unfinished building.
